chapter: Sidemen, mixed bands, the Apollo and Lena Horne
title: Playing the Palladium with Joe Comfort and Stuff Smith
summary: Management made clear a mixed band was unwelcome but did not notice bassist Joe Comfort; Barnet describes a City College date there with Stuff Smith.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: But the time when you couldn't play it was when it was operated as a full time band place where the Palladium hired the bands. When you later played it didn't you say that you played for another promoter?

Oh, yeah. Sterling Way was the manager there. We played a private party in there and we had been playing -- well, I played the Palladium when it was a week's job, and then I also played it when it was five days, and then I played it when it got down to three, and I played it when

it got down to two. One of these times when we were down, I think it was to three days a week they were going, one other day there we played an engagement for City College of Los Angeles, and I had Stuff Smith there and Joe Comfort in the band, and I went up to Sterling Way and I said, "Well," I said, "here we are. Stuff Smith's here and Joe Comfort's here and there isn't anything you can do about it, baby." And he said, "Well, it isn't me anyway. It's the policy of the owners."
And the Hollywood Chamber of Commerce, probably.

Which used to be a terrible restrictive element in Hollywood. But when you finally did play it was when you were working with the Palladium management you couldn't play with a mixed band. Is that right?
No, they made it very clear that I wasn't welcome if I was going to have a mixed band.
So you just didn't tell them about Joe Comfort.
Well that particular time I wasn't working for them. I was working for City College of Los Angeles.
Oh, I thought you said that -- you told me earlier in the evening that you had already taken Joe Comfort in there.
Well, Joe Comfort had been in there. He'd been in there with me. He'd been in there with Harry James. He'd been in there with many bands. So that wasn't any big deal.
They didn't know, or it wasn't obvious enough to them that they cared to make an issue out of it.
But they didn't want anybody coming in featuring Roy Eldridge and -- or Peanuts Holland or Cat Anderson or somebody like that, you know, somebody that was quite obvious.
They're all right so long as they don't show.
